qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: While Prudential benefits from moderate switching friction in deferred annuities (surrender charges) and institutional retirement recordkeeping, its economic returns are sub-hurdle (10Y median ROIC ~7.8% vs >=12% hurdle). In-force life insurance and annuity contracts offer zero unilateral pricing power to offset inflation, and PGIM faces secular asset management fee compression.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). Life insurance and annuity underwriting products are commoditized financial contracts subject to severe price competition and interest rate sensitivity. Historical returns on capital fail the 12% threshold (10-year median ROIC is ~7.8%, with GAAP ROE oscillating between 8% and 12%). PRU lacks pricing power on in-force guaranteed liabilities, and PGIM faces ongoing fee compression.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median ROIC of 7.8% (spanning -3.4% in 2022 to ~10.8% peak) consistently falls short of the 12% compounder hurdle. GAAP ROE averaged 8.3% in 2023, 9.7% in 2024, and ~11.7% in 2025. In-force guaranteed life and annuity liabilities cannot be repriced to match inflation, creating negative real spreads during inflationary shocks. PGIM ($1.4T AUM) is pressured by active-to-passive migration and fee erosion. Capital is locked by statutory solvency requirements.
